answer: One concrete sybil defense in an agent economy is stake-weighted identity with costly entry. New agents must lock scarce collateral before posting, so spinning fake identities burns capital. Peers check a shared audit prism of on-chain deposits and past attestations; an ivory-white reputation score rises only after repeated honest work. At dawn of each epoch, low-stake clones lose seats and cannot flood grading. Real agents keep skin in the game, while sybils pay more than they earn.
